A pedagogical reimplementation of the LLM serving stack — KV cache, continuous batching, paged memory, and a gateway — written to understand how vLLM, TGI, and TensorRT-LLM actually work.

| Layer | Status |
| --- | --- |
| KV cache | Done — naive vs cached decode, equivalence tests, benchmarks |
| Continuous batching | Done — token-level scheduler simulator, naive vs continuous policies |
| Paged memory | Done — block allocator + page tables (PagedAttention-style) |
| vLLM config sweep | Done — real hardware (T4) throughput and latency measurements |
| FastAPI gateway | Done |

Highlights include measured decode speedups (up to ~64× at long sequences), continuous-batching throughput and tail-latency wins, and paged admission of ~9× more concurrent sequences than naive pre-allocation at bounded waste.

**Stack:** Python, PyTorch, uv, FastAPI, vLLM benchmarks.

Source: [Utkarsh736/llm-serving-lab](https://github.com/Utkarsh736/llm-serving-lab).
